label: Thomas Aquinas, Summa theologiae I q.2 a.3…: A mover other than the moved thing that is itself…
locator: I q.2 a.3 co., prima via: quia moventia secunda non movent nisi per hoc quod sunt mota a primo movente
interpretation: The explicit per se (essentially ordered) premise. Moventia secunda are read as moved movers whose moving depends here and now on their being moved, as in the instrumental stick and hand example. The formal statement covers every distinct mover that is moved in any respect; it is therefore the strongest premise of the reconstruction and the natural target of objections (for example a mover moved in an irrelevant respect). The formal premise only says when a link is MovesAsMoved, not when it fails to be one. That a per accidens series, such as a father who begets and was himself begotten, is not a per se series belongs to the intended reading, not to the premise; Aquinas admits that such series could be infinite (ST I q.46 a.2 ad 7).
